profile.headline: Software Engineer @ Box | Content migration, PHP, JavaScript, React, Solidity, Rust, Python
profile.summary:
I am a Software Engineer at Box, a leading cloud content management company that empowers businesses to share, manage, and collaborate on their files. I work in the SWAT department, a team of eight engineers that handles complex and urgent issues related to content migration for various types of customers, from personal accounts to tier 1 clients.

I use PHP, SQL, GCP, and the command line to write, debug, update, and test code and scripts that facilitate the migration process, ensuring quality, efficiency, and customer satisfaction. I also collaborate with other departments and stakeholders, such as QA, product, and sales, to communicate and resolve any technical problems or feedback. 

In addition to my engineering skills, I have a strong interest and background in Political Science and International Relations, which I studied at Diablo Valley College and am currently pursuing at University of California, Davis. I have a keen understanding of political theory, national security, and global affairs, and how they relate to technology and innovation. I am passionate about learning new things and applying them to my work and life.

I am also fluent in Spanish and English, and have experience in retail sales, working at Tommy Bahama and Foot Locker, where I built lasting friendships and learned valuable customer service and communication skills. I am a motivated, adaptable, and collaborative professional who strives to deliver excellence and value to my team and organization.



¡Hola! También hablo español, originalmente conocido como castellano. Soy graduado de Diablo Valley College con un diploma en Ciencias Políticas. Trabajo en una empresa de nube llamada Box como ingeniero de sistemas. En nuestro día a día, utilizamos diferentes herramientas y programas para facilitar la migración de contenido en el producto de Box. Estas incluyen lenguajes de programación como PHP, JavaScript, SQL y Python, GCP.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
At Box’s SWAT department we work from a Kanban Board that tracks our sprints. A lot of this work is tracked through JIRA and we get work from all kinds of customers that could vary from Personal Accounts, Small Businesses, Tier 2 and Tier 1 customers etc.


- Use SQL GCP and the command line along side Script running to identify and complete issues related to content migration. 


- Use PHP to write code, debug, update, and test any outdated scripts using Git in industry practice in the local dev environment. After the changes meet expectations we move over to our staging environment where either one of us at SWAT tests it in staging or another department does QA testing. Once all the testing and merging is done the code is pushed into production either for our use or for customer use.

-Seeing progress is one of the hardest things in Jiu Jutsu you often may feel like you are making zero progress.

-1 you are training in a room full of students that are learning the same moves as you every day as you progress they also progress.

-2 the only time you go backwards in jiu jutsu is not training at all. (similar to not showing up to work at all)

-3 Prevention, the longer you leave the task of escape the harder it will get. When you can see a problem coming this can save you trouble. An escape is easier in the beginning rather than when your in to deep waters.

-4 Recognition, the better it starts the easier it gets finished. Everything takes a sequence of steps. Two things happen here you have to redo the steps or keep on moving on (not easy). When you take the first step make it matter the better it is the easier the rest will be.

organizations.name: MESA
organizations.description:
MESA is an academic enrichment program that serves students seeking degrees in the Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) fields.
MESA USA is a consortium of statewide MESA programs representing 10 states across the country. MESA USA operates collaboratively to broaden participation and improve academic outcomes for underrepresented students in STEM education. MESA programs combine to serve over 50,000 K-16 students annually.

MESA, is an engineering program that offers numerous advantages for aspiring engineers. One of the key pros of MESA is its commitment to promoting diversity and inclusion in the field of engineering. They provide support and resources to underrepresented students, helping to bridge the gap and create equal opportunities for success.

Another advantage of MESA is its focus on hands-on learning and practical application of engineering concepts. Through various projects and competitions, students get to apply their knowledge and skills to real-world problems, gaining valuable experience and enhancing their problem-solving abilities. MESA also offers mentorship programs and networking opportunities, connecting students with industry professionals who can guide and inspire them on their engineering journey. Overall, MESA is a remarkable program that not only equips students with technical expertise but also fosters a sense of community and empowers them to thrive in the field of engineering.

organizations.name: ACE Mentorship Program of America
organizations.description:
Founded in 1994, the ACE Mentor Program of America (ACE) is a free, award-winning, afterschool program designed to attract high school students into pursuing careers in the Architecture, Construction and Engineering industry, including skilled trades. ACE is a federation of more than 75 affiliates (chapters), operating in 38 states and Canada, and largely based in metropolitan areas. A national office supports the affiliate programs.

Over 10,000 students participate annually, drawn from approximately 1,450 high schools.
The majority of ACE students (69%) are minority, and over 40% are female.
One-quarter of ACE seniors entering college are first generation students.
More than 4,100 volunteer industry professionals mentor student teams through a 35-hour-long simulation of designing and constructing a project.
Approximately $2.5 million in scholarships are awarded annually to high school seniors and alumni studying to pursue industry-related careers.
ACE also offers students summer camp and internship opportunities.
